transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’ve just been feeling really restless. Like I’m kind of wound too tight and can’t quite settle, even when I’m supposed to be sitting calmly in a meeting, or painting, or doing yoga. It’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should come in.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different things?
Not really… I mean, I worry about normal things, I guess. Work, stuff at home. But I wouldn’t say it’s a lot of different things all the time.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energized or up compared with your normal self?
Um… not really, no. I have times where I feel keyed up or restless, but I wouldn’t say unusually energized or “up” compared to normal.
Did this restlessness start after a specific stressful event or major life change?
Kind of. It’s been harder to manage for… a little over two years, I guess. Around when the conflicts with my in-laws started taking up more of our evenings.
When the conflict with your in-laws eases up, does the restlessness get noticeably better?
Maybe a little, but it doesn’t really go away. I still feel kind of wound too tight, even when I’m doing something that’s supposed to be calm, like sitting in a meeting or trying to do yoga.
Did you have this same kind of restless, hard-to-sit-still feeling as a child?

Yeah… I think so. I remember in elementary school getting notes sent home because I’d keep getting out of my seat, talking over other kids, or blurting out answers before the teacher was even done asking.
As a teenager, were you still having trouble staying seated or waiting your turn?

I don’t remember the teen years that clearly. I just know even now, if something runs long—like a meeting or a tense dinner with my in-laws—I start finding excuses to get up, like getting water or checking on something, instead of just staying seated.
When you were a child, did these getting-out-of-seat or blurting-out problems happen at home too, or only at school?
I’m not really sure. I remember school more clearly because teachers made a point of it. At home… I don’t know, I don’t have a clear memory of whether it was the same.
As a child, did this getting-out-of-seat or blurting-out behavior cause problems for you anywhere outside of school?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember it causing problems outside of school… at least nothing that stands out to me now.
Do you often have trouble finishing tasks because your mind drifts off or you get distracted?
I’m not sure. I mean, I get distracted sometimes, but I don’t know that I’d say it often keeps me from finishing things.
As a child, did this restless or blurting behavior ever get you into trouble in activities outside of school, like sports, clubs, or with friends?
I don’t really remember anything like that. I might’ve been a bit restless, but I can’t think of getting in trouble for it in sports or with friends.
As a child, did your restlessness or blurting ever cause problems at home?
I don’t really know. I can’t think of anything specific at home, not anything that caused a real problem.
When you feel restless, is it usually because your mind is stuck worrying and you can’t turn the worry off?
Not really worry, no. It’s more like… I just feel wound up, like I can’t fully settle, even when I’m supposed to be sitting calmly in a meeting or doing something quiet like painting or yoga.
Does this restlessness cause problems for you in more than one part of your life now?

Yes… I think so. At work it’s caused some issues with purchase orders, like things needing correction and my planning coordinator having to look things over more. And at home, family dinners can get tense because people feel like I’m talking over them.
Do you often make careless mistakes because you rush through details?

Yes… sometimes. I’ll think I checked a vendor spreadsheet closely, but then my planning coordinator will catch something—like a SKU I transposed, or a freight charge I missed, or the wrong quantity ending up on the purchase order. It’s embarrassing.
Outside of work and family dinners, do you also have this same trouble sitting still or interrupting people in other situations?
Yes… it’s not just work or dinners. Even in quieter things, like if I’m painting or trying to do yoga, I feel sort of wound too tight. Like I should be able to sit calmly, but I can’t fully settle.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on what someone is saying, even when you’re trying to listen?

Yes… that does happen. In sourcing meetings, or even at the dinner table, I can be looking right at someone while they’re asking me something, and then I realize I only caught the last part. I usually have to ask them to repeat it.
Before you turned 12, were these problems with sitting still, blurting things out, or losing focus already happening?

Yes… I think so. I remember in elementary school getting notes sent home because I kept getting out of my seat, talking over other kids, or answering before the teacher was even done asking. It was… a thing, I guess.
Before age 12, did these problems happen in more than one setting, such as both at school and at home?
I’m not really sure. I remember school more clearly, because there were notes and comments. Home is… harder to say. I don’t really have a clear memory of whether it was the same there.
Before age 12, do you remember these same problems causing trouble with friends?
I don’t really remember that clearly. I had friends, but whether those same issues caused problems with them… I’m not sure. That part’s kind of fuzzy.
